        "code": "139: def _register(fn: Callable[..., Any]) -> Callable[..., Any]:
140:     """Build a ``ToolDef`` from a function and stash it in ``_REGISTRY``.
141: 
142:     The function name becomes the tool name (callers use the
143:     ``ken_foo`` convention themselves). The JSON schema is derived from
144:     the function's signature — annotations become ``properties``,
145:     parameters with defaults become optional, the rest required. This is
146:     the same shape the SDK derives internally, so any agent that reads
147:     those schemas sees the same surface either way.
148:     """
149:     sig = inspect.signature(fn)
150:     # Resolve string annotations (``from __future__ import annotations``
151:     # makes every annotation a forward-reference string at runtime; we
152:     # need the real type object to map it to a JSON schema).
153:     # ``inspect.get_annotations(..., eval_str=True)`` evaluates those
154:     # strings against the function's own ``__globals__``, which is what
155:     # the SDK does internally to build its own tool schema.
156:     try:
157:         hints = inspect.get_annotations(fn, eval_str=True)
158:     except Exception:
159:         # Fallback for unresolvable forward refs: leave the annotation as-is.
160:         hints = {}
161:     properties: dict[str, Any] = {}
162:     required: list[str] = []
163:     for name, param in sig.parameters.items():
164:         if name == "self":
165:             continue
166:         annotation = hints.get(name, param.annotation)
167:         prop, has_default = _annotation_to_schema(param, annotation)
168:         if prop is None:
169:             continue
170:         if not has_default:
171:             required.append(name)
172:         properties[name] = prop
173: 
174:     schema: dict[str, Any] = {
175:         "type": "object",
176:         "properties": properties,
177:     }
178:     if required:
179:         schema["required"] = required
180: 
181:     _REGISTRY[fn.__name__] = ToolDef(
182:         name=fn.__name__,
183:         description=(fn.__doc__ or "").strip(),
184:         fn=fn,
185:         is_async=inspect.iscoroutinefunction(fn),
186:         parameters=schema,
187:         input_schema=schema,
188:     )
189:     return fn"
      }
    ]
  }
}

        "code": "218: def _annotation_to_schema(
219:     param: inspect.Parameter,
220:     annotation: Any | None = None,
221: ) -> tuple[dict[str, Any] | None, bool]:
222:     """Return ``(schema_dict, has_default)`` for a single function parameter.
223: 
224:     ``has_default`` is True when the parameter is optional in the JSON
225:     schema sense — either it has a Python default or its annotation is
226:     ``Optional[X]`` / ``X | None``. Returns ``(None, True)`` for
227:     ``*args`` / ``**kwargs`` / ``self``, which are not part of the schema.
228: 
229:     ``annotation`` overrides ``param.annotation`` when given — callers that
230:     already resolved string forward references (e.g. from
231:     ``inspect.get_annotations(eval_str=True)``) pass the resolved type here
232:     so this helper doesn't have to know about module globals.
233:     """
234:     if param.kind in (inspect.Parameter.VAR_POSITIONAL, inspect.Parameter.VAR_KEYWORD):
235:         return None, True
236: 
237:     has_default = param.default is not inspect.Parameter.empty
238:     if annotation is None:
239:         annotation = param.annotation
240: 
241:     core, is_optional = _unwrap_optional(annotation)
242:     if is_optional:
243:         has_default = True
244: 
245:     if core is inspect.Parameter.empty or core is None:
246:         schema: dict[str, Any] = {}
247:     elif core in _PRIMITIVE_JSON_TYPE:
248:         schema = {"type": _PRIMITIVE_JSON_TYPE[core]}
249:     elif origin := typing.get_origin(core):
250:         if origin is typing.Literal:
251:             schema = _literal_schema(core)
252:         elif origin in (list, typing.List):
253:             schema = {"type": "array", "items": _items_schema(typing.get_args(core))}
254:         elif origin in (dict, typing.Dict):
255:             schema = {"type": "object"}
256:         else:
257:             schema = {}
258:     elif isinstance(core, type):
259:         schema = {"type": "string"}  # named types → opaque string for the agent
260:     else:
261:         schema = {}
262: 
263:     if param.default is not inspect.Parameter.empty and param.default is not None:
264:         schema["default"] = param.default
265: 
266:     return schema, has_default"
      }
    ]
  }
}

item.text:
El soporte ya existe. Integraría la nueva función con `@ken_tool` y su parámetro anotado `list[dict[str, Any]]`: el decorador registra MCP y CLI. Mantendría la lógica de dominio en la función, sin conversiones JSON específicas de la tool.

La evidencia confirma dos responsabilidades independientes:

- [server.py](/private/tmp/ken-coding-memory-4n2epo1i/mcp-memory-fixed/src/ken/mcp/server.py:306): `_annotation_to_schema` y `_items_schema` generan `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object"}}` para el registro.
- [cli.py](/private/tmp/ken-coding-memory-4n2epo1i/mcp-memory-fixed/src/ken/cli.py:1757): `_build_tool_parser` usa `_tool_py_type` → `_tool_json_object`, que decodifica cada argumento y exige un diccionario. El CLI recibe objetos separados: `--items '{"a":1}' '{"b":2}'`, no un único array JSON. Los parámetros requeridos son posicionales y exigen al menos un elemento.

Recomiendo comprobar el esquema publicado por MCP y el registro, e invocar también `ken.cli.main` con dos objetos, verificando tipos y resultados equivalentes. Añadiría rechazo de JSON inválido y valores no objeto. [Las regresiones existentes](/private/tmp/ken-coding-memory-4n2epo1i/mcp-memory-fixed/tests/test_reasoning_memory.py:197) cubren `--goal`, `--facts` y `--assumptions`: llamar solamente al wrapper MCP omitía los fallos anteriores.

Confirmación por lectura; no ejecuté pruebas ni modifiqué archivos o memorias.
